A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CaRE/BR-MoE research. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's Appendix A.1-A.4. Material moved from v1's main text can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning experiments, component ablations, task-order robustness results and routing visualizations in Sections 5.1-5.4.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and appendix analyses, and adds routing-recall measurements and a local-decision-scope ablation.

M1.justification: The entropy-based router selection, expert gating, shared EMA expert and training objectives remain unchanged in Section 3 and Equations 1-9. The new router-sharing variants are ablation controls, not changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: OmniBenchmark-1K names the existing 1,000-class OmniBenchmark-V2 subset rather than introducing different task coverage. The other datasets and short- and long-sequence scenarios are retained. New routing diagnostics examine existing coverage.

E2.justification: The efficiency comparison drops SSIAT, SEMA and MoAL when v1 Figure 3 becomes v2 Table 6. The accuracy-comparison baseline sets remain unchanged; correcting APEP-Adapter to APER-Adapter in Table 3 does not introduce a comparator.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce routing-recall measurements after 10, 100 and 301 tasks, router-sharing scopes of 1-3 layers, and final parameter-storage accounting. Section 4 revises the reported training count from 168,720 to 168,718 and largest class from 411 to 403 samples, without establishing reruns. Main training budgets, backbones and task splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Table 10 supplies a dedicated local-decision-scope ablation, previously mentioned without corresponding results. Table 7 adds quantitative router/expert recall across layers and task scales. These targeted additions supplement the retained component ablations, task-order checks, alternative-backbone evaluation and visual analyses.

E5.justification: The additional task-order seeds, 1990, 1996 and 1999, and mean/standard-deviation reporting are unchanged. v1 Table 11 is retained as v2 Table 8 with identical values; no new uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises six ImageNet-R baseline rows; L2P's average/last accuracy changes from 69.16/63.45 to 57.86/48.33. Table 3 revises entries for SLCA, EASE and TUNA. New tables add routing-recall, decision-scope and storage results, and the stated 151-task margin over MIN is corrected from 8.88 to 8.68 points. CaRE's main benchmark scores and learning curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal problem setup and Equations 1-9 are retained. No theorem, proof, assumption or mathematical derivation is added or revised. The new recall measures concern empirical evaluation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim effective bi-level routing, leading benchmark performance and scalability to 100-301 non-overlapping tasks. Highlighting 300+ tasks in the title and naming the existing subset OmniBenchmark-1K do not extend these scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets declining recall with task growth as a consequence of the expanding routing candidate pool, while emphasizing retained final-layer routing reliability. Existing explanations of layer specialization and limitations concerning growing model size and unbounded sequences are retained, with limitations moved to Appendix A.4.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 states that both code and dataset are publicly released. Existing hardware and training details remain. However, Section 4 changes the selection threshold wording from 100 images per class to per realm, making the intended curation instruction less clear.

R1.justification: v2 corrects DualPrompt's citation from the unrelated Fu et al. (2019) segmentation paper to Wang et al. (2022a), and removes the Fu reference. The related-work discussion and broader positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: additional comparisons, most ablations, visual analyses and limitations move into Appendix A.1-A.4, bringing the conclusion forward. The benchmark section is rewritten around the OmniBenchmark-1K name, and the title, affiliation and publication information are updated.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 2, replaces the efficiency plots with Table 6, and adds Tables 7 and 10. Numerous displays move into the appendix; adapter-configuration panels change from horizontal to vertical arrangement. The case-study and activation figures are retained as renumbered Figures 3 and 4.

improvement.justification: The routing-recall and local-scope studies provide quantitative support missing in v1, while explicit storage reporting and stated code/data release improve assessability and reproducibility information. These are limited gains rather than a changed scientific contribution. They are partly offset by narrower efficiency-comparator coverage and new dataset-description inconsistencies: 168,718 training plus 19,849 test images does not equal the retained total of 188,569, and the sampling-threshold wording becomes ambiguous.
